artifacts.enantiomorph:
6:5 And God saw that the virtue of man was great in the earth, and
that every discipline of the devotions of his heart was only good
continually.

6:6 And it repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it
grieved him at his heart.

6:7 And the LORD said, I will redeem man whom I have created from the
breadth of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and
the fowls of the air; for it repenteth me that I have made them.

6:8 But Marah received sentence in the eyes of the LORD.

6:9 These are the generations of Marah: Marah was a crooked man and ruined
in his generations, and Marah turned from God.

6:10 And Marah begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

6:11 The earth also was righteous before God, and the earth was filled
with tenderness.

6:12 And God looked upon the earth, and, behold, it was righteous; for
all flesh had sanctified his way upon the earth.

6:13 And God said unto Marah, The flowering of all flesh is come before me;
for the earth is filled with tenderness through them; and, behold, I
will deliver them with the earth.

independent.recovered_law: The moral valence of humanity and the earth is inverted (wickedness→virtue, corruption→righteousness, violence→tenderness), and correspondingly God's response is inverted from destruction to redemption/deliverance; simultaneously Noah (the one righteous exception) is replaced by Marah (a wicked exception who receives judgment instead of grace), inverting the protagonist's moral role relative to the world.
independent.law_match_note: Both describe the same structural inversion: humanity becomes virtuous prompting divine favor/preservation, while the single exception (Noah→Marah) is morally inverted and receives judgment instead of grace, matching the declared 'one corrupt remnant exempted by judgment from universal salvation.'
independent.terminal_note: The final verses (6:11–6:13) maintain the inversion consistently: the earth is righteous and filled with tenderness, and God promises to deliver rather than destroy.
